title: Statistics and Statistical Analysis
subtitle: Read graphs and scatterplots, interpret regression models, compare trends, and make careful predictions.

materi.judul: Read the graph before the trend

isi.content: A graph is a mathematical representation, not just a picture. Before interpreting a trend, identify the variables, units, axis labels, scale, and interval size.

rows: Change across an ordered variable, often time
Rows, columns, totals, and conditional counts
Association, outliers, and line of best fit

isi.content: Never compare graph values before checking whether the axes use the same units and scale.
A scatterplot displays paired numerical data as points. The overall pattern may show a positive association, negative association, or little to no association.

items.title: No clear association
items.content: The points do not follow a consistent upward or downward pattern.

isi.content: Association does not prove causation. A third variable or the study design may explain why two variables move together.

materi.judul: Linear models and line of best fit

isi.content: \[\hat{y}=mx+b\]
A line of best fit summarizes the general pattern in a scatterplot. The symbol \(\hat{y}\) represents a predicted value rather than necessarily an observed data point.

items.title: Slope \(m\)
items.content: The predicted change in \(y\) for each one-unit increase in \(x\).

items.title: Y-intercept \(b\)
items.content: The predicted value of \(y\) when \(x=0\), if that input is meaningful.

isi.title: Example: interpret a model
isi.content: For \(\hat{y}=4x+12\), the slope 4 means each one-unit increase in \(x\) predicts a 4-unit increase in \(y\). At \(x=7\), the predicted value is \(4(7)+12=40\).

materi.judul: Slope and average rate of change

isi.content: The average rate of change is the change in the dependent variable divided by the change in the independent variable. Include units in the final interpretation.

isi.title: Example: estimate a negative slope
isi.content: A line runs approximately from \((0,14)\) to \((13,0)\). Its slope is \(\dfrac{0-14}{13-0}=-\dfrac{14}{13}\approx-1.1\).

isi.title: Example: average rate
isi.content: If a bird spends 6 hours in flight on January 13 and 15 hours on January 15, the average rate is \(\dfrac{15-6}{2}=4.5\) hours per day.
A negative slope describes a decreasing prediction, not a negative amount of the measured quantity.
If every observed y-coordinate is multiplied by a constant \(k\), the slope and y-intercept of the corresponding linear model are also multiplied by \(k\).
\[y=mx+b\quad\Longrightarrow\quad ky=kmx+kb\]

isi.title: Example: scale every y-value
isi.content: If data set E has model \(y=12+1.5x\) and every y-coordinate is multiplied by 3.9, then the new model is \(y=3.9(12+1.5x)=46.8+5.85x\), approximately \(y=46.8+5.9x\).
Scaling only the y-values changes both the slope and intercept. Scaling only x-values would require a different analysis.

rows: Adds approximately the same amount each interval.
Changes by approximately the same percentage or factor.

isi.title: Example: identify the model type
isi.content: If an investment increases by 0.49% of its previous value each year, the change depends on the current amount. The appropriate model is increasing exponential.
A percentage change describes multiplication by a factor. A fixed numerical change describes addition and is typically linear.

items.title: Interpolation
items.content: Predicting within the observed range of x-values. This is usually more reliable.

items.title: Extrapolation
items.content: Predicting outside the observed range. The relationship may change beyond the data.

items.title: Outlier
items.content: A point that is unusually far from the general pattern.

isi.title: Example: an unreliable prediction
isi.content: If a line model is built from advertising amounts between USD 2,000 and USD 8,000, predicting the outcome at USD 25,000 is extrapolation and may be unreliable.
A model can make a numerical prediction outside the data range, but the prediction should be treated cautiously.
Some questions depend on a graph or table. If a visual and a written statement conflict, identify the conflict instead of inventing precision that the information does not support.

items: Use only values that are clearly labeled or supported by the scale.
Distinguish a flat segment from a slowly changing segment.
Check whether the time interval in the text matches the interval shown.
For a line of best fit, do not assume every observed point lies exactly on the line.

isi.content: When a graph is low-resolution or incomplete, state what can be concluded confidently and avoid unsupported exact values.

items: Identify the graph type, variables, units, and scale.
Use two clear points to estimate slope or average rate of change.
Interpret the intercept only when \(x=0\) has meaning.
Distinguish observed values, predicted values, and residuals.
Do not infer causation from association alone.

latihan.question: A scatterplot shows a strong negative linear pattern, approximately from \((0,9.6)\) to \((5,0.7)\). Which equation is the most appropriate linear model?
discussion: The slope is negative because the pattern decreases.
Using the approximate point at \(x=0\), the y-intercept is about 9.6, so the intercept should be positive and close to 10.1.
Choice B has a negative slope and positive intercept, so it is the appropriate model.

latihan.question: The number of solar-panel installations in five cities is shown in a graph. If the total number of installations is 27,500, what is an appropriate label for the vertical axis?
options: Number of installations in tens of thousands
discussion: A total of 27,500 installations is naturally represented using values in the thousands.
A vertical-axis label such as “number of installations in thousands” allows the total to be represented as 27.5.
The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: A graph shows Marilyn's distance from her campsite during a three-hour hike. She stopped for 90 minutes to eat lunch. Based on the graph description, which time is most consistent with the end of lunch and the continuation of the hike?
discussion: A stop is represented by a flat segment because the distance from the campsite does not change.
The source graph indicates that the flat segment ends at approximately 1:40 P.M.
Therefore, choice C is the intended answer.

latihan.question: A graph shows total music-album sales, in millions, each year from 1997 through 2009. Which best describes the general trend?
options: Sales generally increased each year since 1997.
Sales generally decreased each year since 1997.
Sales increased until 2000 and then generally decreased.
Sales generally remained steady from 1997 through 2009.
discussion: The described graph rises during the early years and then trends downward after approximately 2000.
This is a general trend, not a claim that every individual year changes in exactly the same direction.
The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: A graph shows the temperature of a heated cup of coffee immediately after removal from a heat source and at 10-minute intervals. Which could be the initial temperature?
discussion: The initial temperature is the y-value at time 0.
The source graph begins near 195 degrees Fahrenheit.
Therefore, choice D is the closest possible initial temperature.

latihan.question: A line of best fit runs approximately from \((0,14)\) to \((13,0)\). Which is closest to its slope?
discussion: Use the slope formula: \(m=\dfrac{0-14}{13-0}=-\dfrac{14}{13}\).
The decimal approximation is about \(-1.1\).
The correct answer is choice B.

latihan.question: Three insect colonies are treated with different pesticides over eight weeks. Which colonies decreased in size every two weeks after the initial treatment?
discussion: For each colony, compare the plotted size at each successive two-week interval.
The source graph shows a decrease at every interval for colonies I, II, and III.
Therefore, choice D is correct.

latihan.question: A line of best fit decreases approximately from \((0,8)\) to \((10,1)\). Which is closest to the slope?
discussion: The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: Michael swam 2,000 yards on each of 18 days. A scatterplot shows swim time and heart rate with a line of best fit. For a swim taking 34 minutes, the actual heart rate was about how many beats per minute less than the predicted rate?
discussion: At 34 minutes, compare the observed point with the line of best fit.
The source graph shows the actual heart rate approximately 3 beats per minute below the predicted value.
The correct answer is choice C.

latihan.question: A tree's age is estimated by multiplying its diameter by a species growth factor. Which listed species has a growth factor closest to the value estimated from the source scatterplot?
discussion: The source scatterplot's estimated growth factor is closest to 4.5.
Among the choices, red maple has a growth factor of 4.5.
Therefore, choice A is correct.

latihan.question: A scatterplot shows chamber temperature \(y\) in degrees Celsius against time \(x\) in minutes. The points at \(x=5\) and \(x=7\) are approximately \((5,14)\) and \((7,24)\). What is the average rate of change?
discussion: Use the average-rate formula: \(\dfrac{24-14}{7-5}=\dfrac{10}{2}=5\).
The average rate of change is 5 degrees Celsius per minute.

latihan.question: Data set E has a line of best fit \(y=12+1.5x\). Data set F is created by multiplying every y-coordinate by 3.9. Which could be a line of best fit for F?
discussion: Multiply both the intercept and slope by 3.9.
Rounding the slope gives \(y=46.8+5.9x\), choice A.

latihan.question: A bird spends approximately 6 hours in flight on January 13 and 15 hours on January 15. What is the average rate of change from January 13 to January 15?
discussion: The change in flight time is \(15-6=9\) hours.
The time interval is 2 days.
The average rate is \(9\div2=4.5\) hours per day.

latihan.question: Each year, an investment increases by 0.49% of its previous value. Which model best describes the change?
discussion: The change is a percentage of the previous value, so it is multiplicative.
Because the percentage is positive, the quantity increases.
The appropriate model is increasing exponential, choice C.

latihan.question: A scatterplot shows a negative association, with approximate y-intercept 9.4 and slope \(-0.9\). Which equation is most appropriate?
discussion: Use \(y=mx+b\), where \(m=-0.9\) and \(b=9.4\).
Thus, \(y=9.4-0.9x\), choice D.

latihan.question: For \(x>0\), \(f(x)\) equals 201% of \(x\). Which could describe this function?
discussion: The statement means \(f(x)=2.01x\), which is a linear function.
Because the coefficient is positive, it is increasing.
The correct answer is choice D.

additionalPractice.question: Which graph is most appropriate for monthly temperature over one year?
discussion: Monthly temperature is measured across an ordered time variable.
A line graph is appropriate for showing change across time.

additionalPractice.question: A bar graph shows 18 red items and 27 blue items. How many items are shown?
discussion: Add the two category counts: \(18+27=45\).
Therefore, the graph represents 45 items.

additionalPractice.question: What type of graph displays paired numerical variables as points?
discussion: A scatterplot represents paired numerical observations as individual points.
The correct answer is choice C.

additionalPractice.question: A model is \(\hat{y}=4x+12\). Find the predicted value when \(x=7\).
A line runs from \((2,5)\) to \((8,17)\). Find its slope.
A poll reports 52% support with a margin of error of 3%. State the plausible interval.
discussion: Subtract and add the margin of error: \(52\%-3\%=49\%\) and \(52\%+3\%=55\%\).
The plausible interval is 49% to 55%.

additionalPractice.question: A line model is reliable for advertising between USD \(2{,}000\) and USD \(8{,}000\). Why is predicting at USD \(25{,}000\) risky?
additionalPractice.answer: It is extrapolation outside the observed range.
discussion: The prediction at USD 25,000 is outside the interval used to build the model.
This is extrapolation, so the original relationship may not continue at that level.

additionalPractice.question: A data set E has model \(y=10+2x\). Every y-coordinate is multiplied by 4. Write a model for data set F.
discussion: Multiply the entire model by 4: \(4(10+2x)=40+8x\).
Thus, a model for data set F is \(y=40+8x\).

additionalPractice.question: A scatterplot shows a strong negative association. Explain why this does not prove causation.
additionalPractice.answer: A third variable or the study design may explain the association.
discussion: A negative association means the variables tend to move in opposite directions.
It does not show that changing one variable causes the other to change.
A third variable, coincidence, or the study design may account for the pattern.
